title: The Scripture Has Power
observation: While Jesus was on Earth in physical form, He had all the power of God living in Him. He could have called all the armies of Heaven at any point, but He walked in humble submission to show us the way. This passage could be seen as a pro NBA player playing one-on-one with a 5-year-old kid. It is not even close to a fair game. The NBA player would easily defeat the child and maybe even have a hard time using it as a training lesson for others because there would be such a disparity of skill. That is a way to see this interaction between Jesus and the devil. He is not struggling with the devil. He is teaching us. When we are confronted with temptation, we remember God’s Word. If something would cause us to violate God’s Word, we see it for what it is and move on. If it lines up with the freedom found in God’s Word, we step forward. God’s Word is here to help us know Him and enjoy Him forever. We should never see it as a burden. It is the key to lasting joy.
application: Memorize a promise from God’s Word that speaks against the greatest temptation in your life. When temptation comes, quote God’s Word to yourself out loud. Watch what happens.
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for showing us the way.
